title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 3, 'l-adic homomorphisms attached to an abelian family of cycles'. Setting: X is smooth projective of dimension n over an algebraically closed field k, A is an abelian variety, and Z ∈ CH^i(X×A) is a family of codimension-i cycles on X parametrized by A. Here A^i_alg denotes codimension-i cycles algebraically equivalent to 0 modulo rational equivalence; this is the reading under which u_Z can be non-zero.

The family gives two maps.
(1) A Chow-theoretic map u_Z : A(k) → A^i_alg(X), a ↦ Z_a − Z_0. It is a homomorphism by the usual theorem of the cube / regular-homomorphism argument.
(2) An l-adic map, the action of Z as a correspondence from X to A (written ^tZ because Z is viewed as going from A to X): a(^tZ) : H^{2(n−i)+1}(X)(n−i) → H^1(A). Degree check: H^j(X) → H^{j+2i−2n}(A), and j = 2n−2i+1 lands in H^1.

The claim: modulo torsion (with Q_l coefficients), a(^tZ) depends only on u_Z. More precisely, 'Theorem 3.1': u_Z = 0 ⇔ a(^tZ) = 0. The ⇐ arrow carries a '?'. Pencil marginalia say 'dém. pas faite' and 'A-t-on une réciproque?'. The ⇒ direction is really the substantive content of 'depends only on u_Z'; for linear maps the equivalence would amount to 'factors through the image of u_Z', which needs more.

Proof strategy (continued on the next page):
- Choose an ample complete-intersection curve C ⊂ A through 0 and restrict Z to Z' ∈ CH^i(C×X).
- By Lefschetz, H^1(A) → H^1(C) is injective, so a(^tZ) = 0 ⇔ a(^tZ') = 0.
- J(C) → A is surjective ('C(k) → A(k) surjectif' loosely means C(k) generates A(k)), so u_Z = 0 ⇐ u_{Z'} = 0.
- On X×C the Künneth decomposition H^N(X)⊗H^0(C) ⊕ H^{N−1}(X)⊗H^1(C) ⊕ H^{N−2}(X)⊗H^2(C) is algebraic, because the curve's projectors are.
- The extreme components give u = 0 and a = 0, so one reduces to cycles in the middle component (projection and restriction to X vanish).

In modern terms, this asks whether the cohomological (Tate-module) shadow of a family of cycles is controlled by its Chow-theoretic Abel–Jacobi-type map. This is the territory of regular homomorphisms (Samuel), algebraic representatives (Murre), and Bloch's l-adic Abel–Jacobi map on torsion cycles.
errors: The ⇐ direction (a(^tZ)=0 ⇒ u_Z=0) is false in general. Counterexample: X a K3 surface, i = n = 2. Then H^{2(n−i)+1}(X) = H^1(X) = 0, so a(^tZ) = 0 always. But by Mumford (1969), CH_0(X)_0 is huge: the images of Jacobians J(C_t) of ample curves C_t ⊂ X generate it, so some Z ∈ CH^2(X×J(C)) has u_Z ≠ 0. Grothendieck's '?' over ⇐ and 'dém. pas faite' are justified.

The ⇒ direction is correct with Q-coefficients. If all Z_a are rationally equivalent, a Bloch–Srinivas-type decomposition makes Z − (Z_0 × A) rationally (with Q-coefficients) supported on X×D with D ⊊ A. The action into H^1(A) then factors through H^{−1} of a resolution of D, which is 0. Equivalently, it follows from compatibility with Bloch's l-adic Abel–Jacobi map on A[l^∞] → CH^i(X)[l^∞]. The sketched proof does not yet establish it, and the 'modulo torsion' caveat is necessary.

On the next page, after reducing to a cycle in the middle Künneth component of X×C, the condition a(^tZ') = 0 only says the class is homologically trivial. Griffiths/Mumford phenomena show that this does not force u_{Z'} = 0, so the strategy cannot prove ⇐.
Minor: Grothendieck writes C(k) → A(k) 'surjectif'. The correct statement is that C(k) generates A(k), i.e. J(C) → A is surjective. That suffices for u_Z = 0 ⇐ u_{Z'} = 0.

ideas.what: Attaching to a family Z ∈ CH^i(X×A) parametrized by an abelian variety both a Chow homomorphism u_Z: A(k) → A^i_alg(X) and an l-adic map H^{2n−2i+1}(X)(n−i) → H^1(A)
ideas.modern_name: Regular homomorphisms / algebraic representative; l-adic Abel–Jacobi map on Tate modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Samuel (regular homomorphisms, ~1960); Murre (algebraic representative, 1983–85); Bloch (l-adic Abel–Jacobi on torsion cycles, 1979)
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck's 'Standard conjectures' (1969) and the Kleiman exposition; this precise formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Claim that, rationally, the cohomological action of the family depends only on u_Z, with the question whether u_Z = 0 ⇔ a(^tZ) = 0
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the Chow-theoretic and cohomological Abel–Jacobi maps; failure of the converse (infinite-dimensionality of Chow groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford 1969 (failure of converse for 0-cycles); Bloch 1979, Bloch–Srinivas 1983 (forward direction techniques)

ideas.what: Reduction from an abelian variety to an ample curve via Lefschetz injectivity on H^1 and generation of A(k) by C(k)
Algebraicity of Künneth components for X×C, C a curve, used to split the cycle
ideas.modern_name: Künneth projectors of curves (Chow–Künneth decomposition for curves)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether the Chow-theoretic map u_Z of an abelian family of cycles is detected by its l-adic cohomological action, and leaves the proof undone. The forward direction is essentially what Bloch's l-adic Abel–Jacobi compatibility later gives. The converse fails by Mumford's theorem, so the thread was resolved in the literature by others, not as a response to this note.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest: it documents that Grothendieck was probing, around 1965–71, the gap between Chow groups and l-adic cohomology for families. That gap was later made precise by Mumford (1969), Bloch (1979) and Murre. It is not new mathematics for a specialist.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a natural, partly erroneous conjecture-sketch whose correct half is now standard (Bloch, Murre) and whose converse is refuted by Mumford's well-known result. It is historically interesting as a Grothendieck precursor, but nothing here would surprise a specialist or is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the struck-out word before 'famille' is likely 'une'. The title reads 'Homomorphismes l-adiques associés à une famille abélienne de cycles.'

'Je dis que ces homomorphismes ne dépendent que de u_Z, modulo torsion (i.e. à coefficients Q_l!)'. Here 'modulo torsion' is written above the line and 'ces' sits before 'homomorphismes'; the transcription's ordering is slightly scrambled.
'par ex.' reads more like 'par ex.' followed by a struck-out 'donc' and then 'et de façon précise que'. This is acceptable as transcribed.

The pencil marginalia ('?', the circle around 'Théorème 3.1' linked to 'dém. pas faite', the question mark over the double arrow, and 'A-t-on une réciproque') are later annotations, not part of the ink text.
Second-to-last line: 'Z' ∈ A^i_alg(C×X)' (the subscript 'alg' is abbreviated in the image). The crossed-out text reads 'C×X → ... A' replaced by 'X×C → X×A'.
'a(^tZ') : H^{2(n−i)+1}(X)(n−i) → H^1(C)': the exponent's '+1' is partly overwritten in the image, and the '(X)' is struck through.

The last line likely reads 'et comme H^1(A) → H^1(C) est injectif, C(k) → A(k) surjectif, —'. The last symbol could also be 'Alb', i.e. 'C(k) → Alb surjectif', and the word 'surjectif' wraps to the next line.
